---
title: "An endless banner"
subtitle: "Reproducible, and any part can be made on its own"
---

The banner has no last row. It is built from numbered motif slots, 0, 1, 2 and so on forever, and two rules keep it reproducible:

1. **The motif in slot *k* depends only on the seed and *k*.** The computer derives a private random number generator from the pair (seed, *k*), so slot 1000 always gets the same motif, whether or not slots 0 to 999 were ever made.
2. **The stretch between slots *k* and *k*+1 depends only on those two motifs and its own sub-seed.** Each stretch is filled independently. If filling gets stuck, it retries with the next sub-seed without touching the rest.

The border bands repeat with their own period, so they continue forever too. Together this means:

- the same seed and settings always give exactly the same stitches;
- any section, for example rows 50,000 to 50,300, can be generated and knitted on its own;
- a mistake in one stretch can be regenerated without changing the neighbours.

Every random choice in the code goes through one function, `sub_rng(seed, stage, slot)`, which is what makes this work.
